To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a multipass cell can be used to pump ammonia molecules with CO2 laser radiation and that the output power of the resultant radiation is 10--50kW.
we used a multipass cell in optical pumping of NH/sub 3/.
the output power of an NH/sub 3//CO/sub 2/ gas laser can be increased by two-photon pumping of the NH3 molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of laser, the ammonia laser.
the study of the optical pumping of the ammonia molecule and the generation of laser radiation in the infrared region of the spectrum.
the development and application of a novel technique for the optical pumping of ammonia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a new and potentially useful technique for pumping NH/sub 3/, and perhaps other molecules, has been demonstrated.

the authors have demonstrated that the two-photon optical-pumping technique is an effective method for the generation of high power radiation at wavelengths where the single photon absorption cross section is small.
this work is an important contribution to the understanding of the two-photonic excitation of the NH/sub x/ molecule and its application to lasing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new type of ammonia gas laser pumped by double- photon absorption of the CO/sub 2/.
the use of multipass cell for two-photon pumping of NH/sub 3/, which was first proposed and tested in our laboratory, has been confirmed.
we have demonstrated the first laser action of a molecule in the gas phase by two-photon optical excitation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multipass cell can be used to increase the efficiency of optical pumping and the power of the resultant laser radiation by a factor of 100--1000.
it is possible to obtain a stable gain profile for a two-photon pumped ammonia laser.
it should be easy to build an efficient ammonia laser using the CO2 laser as the pump source.
